newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly lose, LSFO pressured.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly lose, LSFO pressured.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were steady to softer again Thursday in sluggish trade, with burgeoning inventories still pressuring the complex despite forecasts for colder East Coast weather this week and next.

"The whole story is inventory. There's a lot of resid in storage and we've had no (cold) weather to date. Based on demand, the picture is bearish," said one cash trader, noting relatively firm crude prices have helped buoy resid.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent tumbled more than 50 cents on the day to about $19 a barrel, pressured by growing low sulphur offerrs, traders said.
NYH paper prices were steady to down slightly, with both January and February now talked in the high-$18 area.
While colder weather should boost utility loads, traders said it will take a while to trim stocks.
"Right now, we're looking to burn some (resid), not buy some," said one eastern utility source, noting electric demand has been soft and most tanks were still relatively full.
NYH 0.3 percent low pour notionally slid 50 cents to the $22.75-23.00 area, while high pour was flat at $20.75-21.00.
High sulphurs in New York again again were unchanged.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent lost another quarter to $18.00-25, while three percent was unchanged at about $16.50.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
New York city gate gas prices fell another 25 cents to the $4.00/mmBtu level despite colder East Coast weather. NYH one percent resid was at a $3.01/mmBtu equivalent.
